13.title: feat(tts): add VoxCPM2 engine support (Apache-2.0, 48kHz, 30 languages incl. Arabic)
13.body:
## Summary

Add **VoxCPM2** (OpenBMB) as a first-class TTS engine in Voicebox, alongside the existing Qwen / Chatterbox / TADA / Kokoro / LuxTTS / F5-TTS backends.

VoxCPM2 is a 2B-parameter, Apache-2.0, 48 kHz TTS model supporting **30 languages including Arabic**, with zero-shot voice cloning, transcript-aligned "ultimate" cloning, and text-prompted voice *design*. Its Python API maps almost one-to-one onto our existing `TTSBackend` protocol, so this is an additive integration rather than an architectural change.

---

## Resources

| What | URL |
|---|---|
| Demo page / samples | https://openbmb.github.io/voxcpm2-demopage/ |
| Source repository | https://github.com/OpenBMB/VoxCPM |
| Model weights (HF) | https://huggingface.co/openbmb/VoxCPM2 |
| PyPI package | https://pypi.org/project/voxcpm/ |
| Our backend protocol | [`backend/backends/__init__.py#L68`](https://github.com/samykabu/voicebox/blob/main/backend/backends/__init__.py#L68) |
| Reference implementation to copy | [`backend/backends/luxtts_backend.py`](https://github.com/samykabu/voicebox/blob/main/backend/backends/luxtts_backend.py) |

---

## The problem we want to fix

Our current engine line-up leaves three real gaps:

1. **Arabic depends on a non-commercial checkpoint.** Our best broad-dialect Arabic option is `habibi-unified`, which is `CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0` (`commercial_use=False`). The commercially-safe alternative, `habibi-msa`, is MSA-only. VoxCPM2 is **Apache-2.0** and covers Arabic, giving us an unrestricted Arabic path for the first time.

2. **No single engine covers both wide multilingual reach and high-fidelity cloning.** Chatterbox covers 23 languages but needs output trimming (`needs_trim=True`). Kokoro is fast but has no cloning at all. LuxTTS is 48 kHz but English-focused. VoxCPM2 is 48 kHz, 30 languages, *and* clones.

3. **We have no voice *design* capability.** Every engine today requires a reference audio sample to produce a custom voice. VoxCPM2 can synthesize a voice from a plain-text description — `"(A young woman, gentle and sweet)Hello!"` — which unlocks voice creation for users who have no recording to clone from.

---

## Features we need to support

### Must have (v1)

- [ ] **New engine `voxcpm`** registered in `TTS_ENGINES`, selectable in the UI exactly like every other engine.
- [ ] **Standard TTS** — `generate(text, ...)` returning `(np.ndarray, 48000)`.
- [ ] **Zero-shot voice cloning** from an existing Voice Profile's reference audio (`prompt_wav_path` + `prompt_text`).
- [ ] **Voice prompt caching** via `get_cache_key` / `cache_voice_prompt`, matching the LuxTTS and F5 backends.
- [ ] **Multi-sample profiles** — implement `combine_voice_prompts` so profiles with several reference clips work.
- [ ] **Seeded / reproducible generation** — honour the `seed` argument through `manual_seed`.
- [ ] **Model download progress** — wrap loading in `model_load_progress(...)` so the Model Management UI shows the download bar.
- [ ] **Load / unload lifecycle** — `unload_model()` must free VRAM via `empty_device_cache`.
- [ ] **Language list** — register supported languages so the language picker filters correctly, with **Arabic explicitly verified end-to-end**.
- [ ] **Graceful unavailability** — VoxCPM2 is CUDA-only (see risks). The engine must be hidden or clearly disabled on machines that cannot run it, rather than failing at generation time.

### Should have

- [ ] **Voice design from text** — expose the `(description)text` prefix through the existing `instruct` field so users can create a voice with no reference audio.
- [ ] **Generation tuning** — map `cfg_value` and `inference_timesteps` to sensible defaults; consider exposing them as advanced settings.
- [ ] **Arabic pronunciation dictionary compatibility** — confirm our diacritics/prefix matching from [PR #11](https://github.com/samykabu/voicebox/pull/11) applies cleanly to VoxCPM2 input text.
- [ ] **Docs** — add VoxCPM2 to [`docs/content/docs/developer/tts-engines.mdx`](https://github.com/samykabu/voicebox/blob/main/docs/content/docs/developer/tts-engines.mdx) and the model-management page.
- [ ] **E2E test** — add a case to `backend/tests/test_all_models_e2e.py`.

### Out of scope for v1

- Streaming synthesis (`generate_streaming`) — our pipeline is chunk-based today; track separately.
- VoxCPM 1.5 / 0.5B variants — ship **VoxCPM2 only**, as a single size. Adding variants pulls in the multi-size plumbing (`engine_has_model_sizes`, the `("qwen", "tada", "f5_tts")` special-case tuples) for no user benefit.
- The optional denoiser (`load_denoiser=True`).

---

## Proposed implementation

The API maps directly onto our protocol:

| `TTSBackend` protocol | VoxCPM2 |
|---|---|
| `load_model()` | `VoxCPM.from_pretrained("openbmb/VoxCPM2", load_denoiser=False)` |
| `generate(text, voice_prompt, seed)` | `model.generate(text=..., prompt_wav_path=..., prompt_text=..., cfg_value=..., inference_timesteps=..., seed=...)` |
| `instruct` | voice design via `(description)` text prefix |
| returns `(audio, sample_rate)` | wav @ `model.tts_model.sample_rate` = 48 kHz |

### Files to touch

**New**
- `backend/backends/voxcpm_backend.py` — ~200 lines, modelled on `luxtts_backend.py`.

**Backend registry** — `backend/backends/__init__.py`
- `TTS_ENGINES` (L214) — add `"voxcpm": "VoxCPM2"`.
- `_get_non_qwen_tts_configs()` (L296) — add the `ModelConfig` (`license_id="Apache-2.0"`, `commercial_use=True`, `size_mb` ≈ 5000, full language list).
- `get_tts_backend_for_engine()` (L798) — add the dispatch branch.

**Validation & services**
- `backend/models.py` — four engine regex patterns at L92, L413, L432, L451.
- `backend/services/profiles.py` L27 — add `voxcpm` to `CLONING_ENGINES`.

**Install & packaging**
- `backend/requirements.txt` — VoxCPM sub-dependencies.
- `justfile` L67-74 (Unix) **and** L120-123 (Windows) — `pip install --no-deps voxcpm`, following the established pattern for chatterbox / hume-tada / f5-tts.
- `backend/build_binary.py` — hidden imports + data collection, mirroring the `kokoro` (L276) and `f5_tts` (L308) entries.

**Frontend** — `app/src`
- `lib/api/types.ts` L84 — engine union.
- `lib/constants/languages.ts` L73 — per-engine language map.
- `components/Generation/EngineModelSelector.tsx`, `components/Generation/FloatingGenerateBox.tsx`, `components/VoiceProfiles/ProfileForm.tsx`, `lib/hooks/useGenerationForm.ts`, `lib/utils/format.ts`, `components/ServerSettings/ModelManagement.tsx`.

---

## Risks & open questions

These need a dependency probe in a scratch venv **before** the backend is written.

1. **CUDA-only.** Upstream states CUDA >= 12.0 and documents no CPU or MPS path. This would be our first engine with **no macOS support at all**, and no CPU fallback. Needs a decision on how the UI presents an engine unavailable on the user's hardware. *Open question: does `voxcpm` actually run on CPU, just slowly?*

2. **Python version ceiling.** `voxcpm` requires Python `<3.13`. Our `requires-python` is `>=3.12` and the justfile falls back to 3.13 when 3.12 is absent — that fallback path would break.

3. **Dependency conflicts.** We pin `numpy<2.0` and `transformers<=4.57.6`. VoxCPM will almost certainly conflict, hence the `--no-deps` install. The full transitive dependency set needs to be enumerated by hand.

4. **Footprint.** ~8 GB VRAM and a multi-GB download — our heaviest engine. Confirm the actual `size_mb` for the Model Management UI.

5. **Frozen build size.** Adding another multi-GB model path affects the PyInstaller bundle; verify the desktop build still produces.

## Fork maintenance note

This is a fork-local feature. Keep the change **additive** — a new backend file plus registry entries — to minimise merge conflicts when syncing from `jamiepine/voicebox` upstream.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] VoxCPM2 appears in the engine picker, downloads with a visible progress bar, and generates 48 kHz audio.
- [ ] A Voice Profile cloned with VoxCPM2 produces recognisable speaker likeness.
- [ ] Arabic generation works and respects the pronunciation dictionary.
- [ ] Model unload returns VRAM to the OS.
- [ ] `just setup` succeeds cleanly on Windows and Linux with the new dependency.
- [ ] The engine degrades gracefully (hidden or disabled with a clear reason) on unsupported hardware.
- [ ] Docs and the E2E test are updated.

<!-- speckit-scope:start -->
## Scope analysis

Effort: **13**

breadth=3: ten must-have behaviours plus three should-haves, spread across a new backend file, the registry sites in backends/__init__.py, four regexes in models.py, one service constant, three install and packaging files, eight frontend files, two docs pages and an E2E case. Each of cloning, caching, multi-sample combining, seeding, download progress, unload, language registration and graceful unavailability is independently testable, which is what makes this broad rather than merely long. integration=3: a multi-GB external model installed --no-deps against two hard pins (numpy<2.0, transformers<=4.57.6) whose transitive set is not yet enumerated; a Python <3.13 ceiling against a justfile fallback to 3.13; a PyInstaller frozen bundle that must still produce; and a cross-component contract gap, since no route exposes TTS_ENGINES and the frontend hardcodes its own engine and language lists, so Principle III's declared-capabilities requirement has no existing mechanism to use. Principle V then pulls in the generated TypeScript client and backend/README.md if an endpoint appears. No unmerged prerequisites, but the internal contract work is real. data_security=0: no data migration, no tenancy, no authorization change and no new sensitive data path. Voice data handling is unchanged because the engine reuses the existing profile and cache plumbing, and the licensing change moves from CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 toward Apache-2.0, which loosens a restriction rather than creating exposure. Scored 0 on evidence, not to lower the total. verification=3: the accelerator matrix is five accelerators across three operating systems and this is the first engine that cannot satisfy all of it, so the unsupported path must be enforced and tested, not merely declared. just setup must be verified on Windows and Linux, the frozen build must be verified separately, Arabic must be verified end to end against the pronunciation dictionary, and each E2E run costs a multi-GB download and roughly 8 GB of VRAM. pytest does not run in CI, so every one of these is a local gate the author must run and attest to in the PR. uncertainty=3: the issue itself states that a scratch-venv dependency probe is required before the backend is written. Four material unknowns are open: whether voxcpm runs on CPU at all, the full transitive dependency list, the real size_mb for the Model Management UI, and how an engine unavailable on the user's hardware should be presented. The last is a design decision the issue explicitly leaves open. Sum 12 maps to 13 points. The score is above 5, which recommends considering decomposition; a four-way split along probe, capability-contract, backend, and frontend-with-docs seams was presented with its tradeoffs. The user reviewed that recommendation and chose to keep the issue whole as a single executable unit. The score is retained honestly at 13 rather than reduced to match that choice.

### Implementation alignment

No prerequisite issues exist; inspect reports ready=true with zero dependencies, zero sub-issues and zero comments. The delta is measured against main at the time of scoping. IMPLEMENTED TODAY: the TTSBackend protocol (backend/backends/__init__.py:68-135) already defines load_model, create_voice_prompt, combine_voice_prompts, generate, unload_model, is_loaded and _get_model_path, so a new engine is additive. LuxTTSBackend (backend/backends/luxtts_backend.py, 184 lines) is a complete working template for a single-size 48 kHz cloning engine and already uses every shared helper the issue names: model_load_progress, empty_device_cache, manual_seed, get_cache_key/cache_voice_prompt and the shared combine_voice_prompts in backends/base.py. The --no-deps install pattern is established four times over in the justfile (chatterbox-tts, hume-tada, f5-tts==1.1.21, habibi-tts==0.1.1) on both the Unix path (justfile:67-74) and the Windows path (justfile:120-123). ModelConfig already carries license_id, commercial_use, languages and size_mb, so the licensing metadata the issue wants has a home. The Arabic licensing gap the issue describes is confirmed: habibi-unified is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 with commercial_use=False (backend/backends/__init__.py:391-401) and habibi-msa is Apache-2.0 but MSA-dialect only (:378-389); both ride engine=f5_tts rather than an engine of their own. REMAINING DELTA: a new voxcpm_backend.py; the registry sites (TTS_ENGINES at :214, a ModelConfig in _get_non_qwen_tts_configs at :296, the dispatch branch at :798, with the Unknown-engine error at :859 deriving from TTS_ENGINES automatically); four identical engine regexes in backend/models.py (:92, :413, :432, :451); CLONING_ENGINES in backend/services/profiles.py:27; install plumbing in backend/requirements.txt, both justfile paths and backend/build_binary.py; eight frontend files; docs and one E2E case. UNRESOLVED ASSUMPTIONS, not implemented behaviour: whether voxcpm runs on CPU at all, the full transitive dependency set required by a --no-deps install, the real on-disk size_mb, and how an engine unavailable on the user's hardware is presented. The issue itself requires a scratch-venv dependency probe before the backend is written; that probe is the first unit of work inside this issue, not a precondition someone else supplies.

### Evidence

- backend/backends/__init__.py:68-135 - the TTSBackend protocol this engine implements in full
- backend/backends/luxtts_backend.py:1-184 - the single-size 48 kHz cloning template to copy, including every shared helper named in the issue
- backend/backends/__init__.py:214-222 - TTS_ENGINES, 8 engines, no voxcpm
- backend/backends/__init__.py:296-311 - the ModelConfig list this engine joins
- backend/backends/__init__.py:798-861 - the dispatch chain and its Unknown-engine error derived from TTS_ENGINES
- backend/backends/__init__.py:378-401 - habibi-msa Apache-2.0 MSA-only versus habibi-unified CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 commercial_use=False: the confirmed Arabic licensing gap this engine closes
- backend/models.py:92,413,432,451 - the four identical engine regexes
- backend/services/profiles.py:27 - CLONING_ENGINES, voxcpm absent
- backend/requirements.txt:12,76 - transformers<=4.57.6 and numpy<2.0, the pins the --no-deps install protects
- justfile:21 - the python3.13 fallback that the voxcpm Python <3.13 ceiling puts at risk
- justfile:67-74,120-123 - the established --no-deps pattern on both platform paths
- backend/pyproject.toml:4 - requires-python >=3.12 is already compatible with the ceiling
- backend/routes/ - no route reads TTS_ENGINES; there is no server-to-client engine availability channel today
- app/src/components/Generation/EngineModelSelector.tsx:23-39 - hardcoded ENGINE_OPTIONS
- app/src/lib/constants/languages.ts:65-74 - hardcoded ENGINE_LANGUAGES map
- app/src/lib/api/types.ts:80-84 - the engine union
- backend/routes/cuda.py:16-22 and app/src/components/ServerSettings/GpuAcceleration.tsx:31-59 - nearest prior art for reporting hardware availability to the UI
- backend/backends/base.py:82-112 - get_torch_device, the accelerator detection a CUDA-only engine consults
- backend/tests/test_all_models_e2e.py and docs/content/docs/developer/tts-engines.mdx - both exist and are the named targets
- .specify/memory/constitution.md - Principle III, Principle IV, Principle V, Accelerator Matrix and Quality Gates all bind this change

### Speckit Specify prompt

```text
GitHub issue #13
Effort: 13

Add VoxCPM2 as a first-class TTS engine in Voicebox so that users get an Apache-2.0, 48 kHz, 30-language engine that can both clone a voice from a sample and design one from a written description.

WHY THIS MATTERS. Three gaps exist today. First, the best broad-dialect Arabic voice in the product, habibi-unified, is licensed CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and is flagged as not permitted for commercial use; the only commercially safe Arabic alternative, habibi-msa, is Modern Standard Arabic only. VoxCPM2 is Apache-2.0 and covers Arabic, which gives the product an unrestricted Arabic path for the first time. Second, no single engine currently offers both wide multilingual reach and high-fidelity cloning: Chatterbox reaches 23 languages but needs output trimming, Kokoro is fast but cannot clone at all, and LuxTTS is 48 kHz but English-focused. VoxCPM2 is 48 kHz, 30 languages, and clones. Third, every engine today requires a recording before a custom voice can exist. VoxCPM2 can synthesise a voice from a plain-text description such as "(A young woman, gentle and sweet)Hello!", which opens voice creation to users who have nothing to clone from.

WHAT USERS SHOULD BE ABLE TO DO. Select VoxCPM2 from the engine picker the same way they select any other engine. Watch it download with a visible progress bar the first time it is needed. Generate 48 kHz speech from text. Clone a voice from an existing Voice Profile, including profiles that hold several reference clips. Get the identical result twice from the same seed. Generate Arabic that respects the pronunciation dictionary. Create a voice from a written description without supplying any audio. Unload the model and get their VRAM back. On a machine that cannot run the engine, see it hidden or clearly disabled with a stated reason, instead of choosing it and hitting a failure at generation time.

WHAT MUST BE SETTLED FIRST. Four questions are open, and a dependency probe in a scratch virtual environment is required before backend code is written, because the answers change the work. Does voxcpm actually run on CPU, just slowly, or is CUDA genuinely mandatory? Upstream documents CUDA 12.0 or newer and no CPU or MPS path, which would make this the first engine in the product with no macOS support at all. What is the complete transitive dependency set, given that the install must use --no-deps to avoid breaking the existing numpy<2.0 and transformers<=4.57.6 pins? What is the real on-disk size, so the Model Management UI reports it honestly: roughly 8 GB of VRAM and a multi-GB download would make this the heaviest engine in the product. And does the Python upper bound of below 3.13 break the setup path? The project floor of Python 3.12 or newer is itself compatible with that ceiling; the actual risk is the setup script's fallback to Python 3.13 when 3.12 is absent.

CONSTRAINTS LEARNED FROM THE EXISTING CODEBASE. The backend protocol every engine implements already covers loading, voice-prompt creation, multi-prompt combining, generation, unloading and load-state reporting, so this integration is additive rather than architectural. LuxTTS is the closest existing engine (single size, 48 kHz, cloning) and is the model to follow; it already uses the shared helpers for load progress, device cache clearing, seeding, prompt caching and multi-sample combining, and the new engine should use the same ones rather than inventing parallel machinery. The --no-deps install pattern is established four times over and exists on both the Unix and the Windows setup paths, so both must be edited together. Engine capability, meaning which languages and which accelerators, must be declared once on the backend and queried by callers: the project constitution forbids expressing engine-specific behaviour as engine-name branching in route handlers or the frontend, and requires a new engine to declare its accelerator support and either degrade to CPU or report unavailability rather than crash. That matters here because no mechanism for this exists yet: nothing in the API layer exposes the engine registry, and the frontend keeps its own hardcoded engine and language lists. If this work adds or changes an API surface, the typed models, the generated client and the backend API documentation must all move in the same change, and the generated client must not be hand-edited. Heavy model libraries must be imported lazily inside functions so application startup does not slow down as engines are added.

SCOPE BOUNDARIES. Ship VoxCPM2 only, as a single model size: no VoxCPM 1.5 and no 0.5B variant, so none of the multi-size machinery is touched. No streaming synthesis; the pipeline is chunk-based today and streaming is tracked separately. No optional denoiser. No transcript-aligned ultimate cloning beyond ordinary zero-shot cloning. Do not migrate the seven existing engines onto any capability mechanism this work introduces: only the new engine needs to use it. Do not remove or replace the existing Arabic models; VoxCPM2 is added alongside them. Do not change the project's Python floor, which would require a constitutional amendment.

KEEP IT ADDITIVE. This repository is a fork that must stay cheaply mergeable with its upstream. Shape the change as a new backend file plus registration entries, and avoid refactors that would complicate future merges.

HOW IT WILL BE JUDGED. The engine appears in the picker, downloads with a visible progress bar and produces 48 kHz audio. A profile cloned with it sounds recognisably like the speaker. Arabic works and respects the pronunciation dictionary. Unloading returns VRAM. Setup succeeds cleanly on both Windows and Linux without disturbing the existing dependency pins, and the packaged desktop build still produces. The engine degrades gracefully on unsupported hardware. Documentation and the end-to-end test suite are updated. Because the Python test suite does not run in continuous integration, the author must run it locally before requesting review and say so in the pull request.

SOURCE. GitHub issue samykabu/voicebox#13, effort score 13, kept whole as a single executable issue by explicit user decision after a four-way decomposition was proposed.
```
